topics.partBanner: Part A · Internet Fundamentals & Information Literacy
topics.title: 1. Web Architecture, Secure Protocols (HTTPS) & Search Syntax
topics.premise: Aviation personnel access weather reports, NOTAMs (Notices to Air Missions), and regulatory mandates across web networks. Understanding URL architecture, encryption padlocks, and search operators is vital for fast, authentic information retrieval.

rows: URL Structure
https://www.dgca.gov.in/rules/car.html
Protocol (https), Subdomain (www), Domain (dgca.gov.in), Path (/rules/car.html)
Identifies exact web resource location; validates official government authenticity
HTTPS & SSL/TLS Padlock
https:// with padlock icon
Encrypts communication between user browser and web server
Guarantees passenger payment details and passport numbers cannot be intercepted in transit
Search Operator: site:
site:dgca.gov.in 'CAR Section 3'
Restricts search results exclusively to the specified official domain
Instantly pulls official Civil Aviation Requirements without commercial blog clutter
Search Operator: filetype:
filetype:pdf 'flight safety circular'
Filters search engine results to return only specific file formats (e.g., PDF)
Directly retrieves downloadable regulatory circulars and safety bulletin PDFs
Search Operator: Quotes ("")
"minimum equipment list" A320
Forces exact phrase matching in the specified order
Finds exact technical regulatory phrases rather than loose disconnected keyword hits
Browser Cache & History
Ctrl + Shift + Delete
Stores temporary web files and visited sites for fast reloading
Clearing cache resolves outdated weather radar loops and stuck flight booking portals

rule.title: The Secure Protocol Rule
rule.text: Never enter passenger credentials, payment card details, or flight dispatch logins on any website showing 'http://' (unsecured HTTP) or browser warning flags. Legitimate airline portals ALWAYS enforce 'https://' with a valid SSL/TLS certificate.

workedExample.title: Worked Example: Rapid Regulatory Lookup for Station Audit
workedExample.text: A station manager needs the latest DGCA circular on baggage compensation guidelines.
steps: Inefficient query: dgca baggage rules in india (returns 500,000 news articles and blogs).
Targeted Boolean query: site:dgca.gov.in filetype:pdf "passenger charter" baggage
Outcome: Result #1 is the exact official DGCA PDF circular with compensation fee tables.
Time taken: 3 seconds versus 20 minutes of filtering through irrelevant blogs.
workedExample.verdict: Advanced Boolean operators turn the search engine into an instant regulatory index.

topics.memoryTrick: U-R-L-S: Uniform Resource Locator Security: Check Protocol, Verify Domain, Restrict with site:, Filter with filetype:.
topics.examTip: In a 3-mark question on web security: Explain that HTTPS uses SSL/TLS encryption to protect sensitive data from eavesdropping (Man-in-the-Middle attacks), whereas HTTP transmits plain text that can be intercepted on open Wi-Fi.

topics.partBanner: Part B · Enterprise Email Communication & Etiquette
topics.title: 2. Professional Email Protocol, CC vs BCC & Passenger Data Privacy
topics.premise: Email is the legal backbone of airline enterprise communication. Misunderstanding CC versus BCC can cause massive data privacy breaches, while poor subject lines can stall ground handling coordination.

rows: To Field
Primary direct recipient(s) expected to take action or respond
To: Station_Manager@skylink.com regarding ramp staffing shortfall
Recipient is directly accountable for resolving the matter
Carbon Copy (CC)
Secondary recipient(s) included for situational awareness (no direct action required)
CC: Duty_Officer@skylink.com, Safety_Lead@skylink.com on incident report
All recipients see each other's email addresses
Blind Carbon Copy (BCC)
Hidden recipient(s); address is completely invisible to other recipients
BCC: 180 delayed passengers when emailing flight delay advisories
MANDATORY FOR PRIVACY: Prevents catastrophic passenger email leaks (GDPR/DPDP violation)
Subject Line
Clear, concise 5-8 word summary with flight/date/action tags
Subject: [URGENT] Flight SL-402 Delay Advisory & Gate Change - 14 Oct
Allows recipients to triage and prioritize urgent operational actions instantly
Email Signature
Standardized block: Full Name, Official Designation, Airline, Contact Details
Rohit Verma | Duty Manager | Ground Ops | Kempegowda Intl Airport
Establishes institutional authenticity and direct telephone contact
Attachment Hygiene
Attaching relevant compressed documentation with clean names
Attaching 'Incident_Report_AI402_14Oct.pdf' (under 10 MB)
Never attach executable files (.exe, .bat) or huge uncompressed archives

rule.title: The Strict BCC Privacy Rule
rule.text: When emailing multiple passengers or external vendors: NEVER put their email addresses in 'To' or 'CC'. ALWAYS use 'BCC'. Placing customer email addresses in CC exposes private contact details to strangers, violating aviation privacy laws and company data policies.

workedExample.title: Worked Example: Drafting an Operational Delay Notice to Passengers
workedExample.text: Draft an official flight rescheduling notice for passengers of Flight 6E 902.
steps: To: ops-notification@skylink.com (generic internal dummy address).
BCC: [List of all 160 passenger email addresses pasted here].
Subject: Operational Advisory: Flight SL 902 (BLR to DEL) Rescheduled - 14 Oct 2026.
Salutation: 'Dear Esteemed Passenger,'

Body: 'Please be advised that due to incoming airspace congestion, Flight SL 902 scheduled for departure at 14:30 hrs has been revised to 16:15 hrs. Gate open at 15:30 hrs. Refreshment vouchers are available at Counter 12.'
Sign-off: 'Sincerely, Ground Operations Team, SkyLink Airways'.
workedExample.verdict: Professional, courteous, operationally clear, and 100% compliant with privacy regulations.

topics.memoryTrick: B-C-C-P-R-I-V-A-C-Y: Blind Carbon Copy Protects Recipient Identity & Vital Aviation Confidentiality.
topics.examTip: A guaranteed exam question: What is the difference between CC and BCC? Answer: CC (Carbon Copy) displays recipient email addresses to everyone on the thread; BCC (Blind Carbon Copy) hides recipient addresses, protecting recipient privacy.

topics.partBanner: Part C · Cloud Drives & Aviation Cyber Safety
topics.title: 3. Cloud Collaboration, Cyber Threats (Phishing/Malware) & MFA Security
topics.premise: Airlines store shared shift handovers and flight plans on cloud drives (OneDrive, Google Drive). Ground workstations are prime targets for cyber attacks; staff must maintain vigilance against phishing, weak passwords, and unauthorized device connections.

rows: Cloud Sharing Permissions
View Only vs Commenter vs Editor permissions
Sharing live ground crew duty roster across terminal teams
Grant 'Editor' only to Duty Supervisors; all other staff receive 'View Only'
Phishing Attack
Fraudulent emails mimicking trusted authorities (DGCA, IT Support) to steal logins
Email pretending to be 'IT Helpdesk' demanding password reset via shady link
Never click links in unexpected emails; verify sender domain; report to Airline Cyber Security
Malware & Ransomware
Malicious software encrypting files or locking workstations for ransom
Infected USB drive inserted into dispatch terminal encrypts flight manifests
Strict policy banning unauthorized USB flash drives; continuous antivirus definitions
Strong Password Criteria
Minimum 12-16 characters: Uppercase, Lowercase, Numbers, and Special Symbols
Securing airline check-in terminal user accounts against brute force attacks
Use passphrase sentences (e.g., 'SkyFly#2026@BLR!Safe'); never reuse passwords
Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
Requires 2+ verification factors: Password + OTP/Authenticator App prompt
Accessing airline crew scheduling portal from mobile or remote tablet
Even if password is stolen in a phishing attempt, attacker cannot log in without the physical OTP token
Public / Apron Wi-Fi Hygiene
Unencrypted open Wi-Fi networks subject to packet sniffing and spoofing
Ground agent checking company flight schedules on airport public Wi-Fi
Always connect via corporate Virtual Private Network (VPN); never disable firewall

rule.title: The Zero-Trust USB & Password Rule
rule.text: 1. NEVER plug personal USB pen drives into airport operational workstations. 2. NEVER share your terminal user password with colleagues or write it on sticky notes. Every agent is legally liable for actions logged under their user ID.

workedExample.title: Worked Example: Identifying a Spear-Phishing Email Attempt
workedExample.text: A ticketing agent receives an email: 'URGENT from DGCA: Your Airport Pass has been revoked. Click here immediately to verify credentials: http://dgca-verification-portal.xyz/login'.
steps: Red Flag 1: False urgency ('Click immediately or pass revoked').
Red Flag 2: Suspicious sender domain (dgca-verification-portal.xyz instead of official dgca.gov.in).
Red Flag 3: Unsecured HTTP link instead of official HTTPS.
Correct Action: Do NOT click the link. Take a screenshot, forward email to airline Cyber Security Ops, and notify supervisor.
workedExample.verdict: Vigilant staff response halts potential cyber intrusion into the airport reservation network.

topics.memoryTrick: P-A-S-S-W-O-R-D: Phishing awareness, Authentication MFA, Share links with expiry, Strong passwords, Wi-Fi security, OS updates, Regular backups, Defense vigilance.
topics.examTip: In a 5-mark question on Cyber Threats: Define Phishing (social engineering email deception), Ransomware (malware that encrypts operational data for ransom), and MFA (two-factor authentication combining something you know + something you have).

quickRevision.rememberThis: HTTPS uses SSL/TLS encryption (padlock icon) to prevent data interception; HTTP transmits plain text.
site: limits search to one domain (site:dgca.gov.in); filetype: filters format (filetype:pdf); quotes enforce exact phrase.
CC reveals email addresses to all recipients; BCC hides addresses to protect passenger personal privacy.

topics.partBanner: Part A · Hardware Architecture & The Von Neumann Model
topics.title: 1. Computer Hardware Architecture & Aviation Workstation Peripherals
topics.premise: Modern airport check-in desks, flight dispatch consoles, and baggage sorters operate on the Von Neumann architecture: Input devices feed data to the Central Processing Unit (CPU), which coordinates with memory and storage to output flight documentation.

rows: Central Processing Unit (CPU)
Fetches, decodes, and executes program instructions via ALU & Control Unit
Processes real-time radar streams, ticket validation, and weight & balance math
Workstation freeze; check-in passenger queues stall
Primary Memory (RAM)
High-speed volatile working memory for active programs and current processes
Holds active flight manifests and passenger reservation sessions open in Amadeus/SITA
Session loss on crash; system slowness if overloaded (thrashing)
Read-Only Memory (ROM)
Non-volatile permanent firmware storing BIOS/UEFI boot sequence
Initiates hardware checks (POST) and boots airport kiosk operating system
Terminal cannot boot or locate operating system drive
Secondary Storage (SSD/NVMe)
Permanent high-capacity non-volatile storage for files and OS
Stores passenger PII archives, historical flight plans, and software binaries
Data corruption; inability to load flight manifests
Input Devices (Barcode/OCR, Keyboard)
Converts human actions and physical travel docs into digital electrical signals
Passport MRZ scanners, boarding pass 2D barcode readers, baggage scale sensors
Manual data entry required; severe check-in delays
Output Devices (Thermal Printers, FIDS)
Translates processed binary data into readable physical or visual formats
Bag-tag thermal printers, Boarding Pass printers, Flight Information Display Screens
Passengers cannot board; bags lack routing tags

rule.title: The Memory Volatility Rule
rule.text: RAM is VOLATILE: all unsaved flight records are wiped immediately if power cuts out. ROM and SSD/HDD are NON-VOLATILE: firmware and saved flight manifests survive reboots and power outages.

workedExample.title: Worked Example: Airport Kiosk Memory Diagnostic
workedExample.text: A self-service check-in kiosk at Bengaluru Airport (BLR) encounters sudden lag when processing baggage tags for Flight 6E 402.
steps: Step 1: The supervisor opens Task Manager (Ctrl + Shift + Esc).
Step 2: CPU utilization is normal at 14%, but RAM usage is pinned at 98% due to an unclosed legacy background reporting tool.
Step 3: Diagnostic: Memory leakage in RAM, not secondary storage failure.
Step 4: Remediation: Terminate the memory-hogging process in Task Manager; RAM utilization drops to 32%, restoring instant barcode printing.
workedExample.verdict: Clear distinction between RAM exhaustion and physical SSD corruption isolates the problem in 30 seconds.

topics.memoryTrick: I-P-O-S: Input (Passport Scan) → Processing (CPU validates seat) → Output (Prints Boarding Pass) → Storage (Logs to Passenger Database).
topics.examTip: Never write that RAM stores files permanently. In a 3-mark question, always define RAM as volatile temporary memory and SSD/HDD as non-volatile secondary storage.

topics.partBanner: Part B · Software Classification & Windows Navigation
topics.title: 2. Software Classifications, Licensing & Windows 11 Enterprise Navigation
topics.premise: Airport operations run on a two-tier software stack: System Software manages the hardware environment and drivers, while Application Software carries out specific business and passenger handling tasks.

rows: System Software
Operating System (OS)
Manages hardware resources, file memory allocation, multitasking, and user interface
Windows 11 Enterprise, Red Hat Enterprise Linux (Radar servers)
System Software
Device Drivers
Translates OS commands into hardware-specific language
BOCA thermal printer driver for boarding pass printing
System Software
Utility Programs
Maintains, secures, and optimizes computer integrity
Windows Defender Antivirus, Disk Cleanup, Task Manager
Application Software
General Purpose
Everyday productivity software for standard administrative office tasks
Microsoft Office 365 (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook)
Application Software
Bespoke / Specialized
Custom enterprise applications engineered for aviation operational workflows
Amadeus Altea DCS, SITA BagManager, Jeppesen FliteDeck Pro
Software Licensing
Proprietary vs Enterprise Volume
Proprietary source code protected; volume licenses deployed across thousands of airport kiosks
Microsoft Volume Licensing Key (VLK) across 250 airport terminal desks

rule.title: The Principle of Least Privilege (Security Rule)
rule.text: Ground operations staff and ticketing agents must only operate with Standard User OS rights. Administrative privileges are restricted to IT Engineers to prevent unauthorized software installations or security breaches.

topics.memoryTrick: S-A-U-D: System software manages the machine; Application software solves the user task; Utility protects the system; Drivers translate hardware.
topics.examTip: When asked for essential Windows keyboard shortcuts in exams: Win + E opens File Explorer; Ctrl + Shift + Esc directly opens Task Manager; Win + L locks the terminal (vital when stepping away from passenger data); Alt + Tab switches active windows.

rule.title: The Standard File Naming Convention Rule
rule.text: Format: [Date]_[FlightNumber]_[DocumentType]_[Version].[extension]. Example: 20261014_AI402_LoadTrimSheet_v1.0.pdf. Never use spaces, question marks, or vague names like 'Doc1.docx'.

rows: Equals Sign (=)

rule.title: The Formula Initialization Rule
rule.text: Every formula in Excel MUST begin with an equals sign (=). Without '=', typing '100+50' in cell A1 will display the literal characters '100+50' instead of calculating 150.

workedExample.title: Worked Example: Calculating Takeoff Weight & Payload Margin
workedExample.text: Calculate payload and margin for Flight AI-802 with Max Takeoff Weight (MTOW) of 75,000 kg.
steps: Given: Dry Operating Weight (DOW) = 42,000 kg (in B2); Fuel = 14,000 kg (in B3); Cargo = 5,500 kg (in B4); Passenger Weight = 11,200 kg (in B5).
Step 1: Calculate Total Takeoff Weight in B6: =B2 + B3 + B4 + B5 → 72,700 kg.
Step 2: In B7, calculate Available Margin: =75000 - B6 → 2,300 kg safety margin.
Step 3: Verification: Formula executes cleanly without PEMDAS ambiguity.
workedExample.verdict: Structured arithmetic proves the aircraft is 2,300 kg under MTOW and certified safe for departure.

topics.memoryTrick: P-E-M-D-A-S: Parentheses → Exponents → Multiplication → Division → Addition → Subtraction.

rows: Relative Referencing
Row numbers update (A3*B3, A4*B4)
Calculating row-by-row baggage fees for individual passengers

Locks column A or row 1 only

SUM()

=AVERAGE(range)
Calculates mathematical mean of numeric cells

COUNT() vs COUNTA()
=COUNT() / =COUNTA()
COUNT counts numbers; COUNTA counts all non-empty cells
COUNT counts total paid fares; COUNTA counts total passenger names checked in

Returns lowest and highest numeric value

rule.title: The Dollar Sign ($) Anchor Rule
rule.text: The dollar sign ($) locks whatever follows it. $A$1 locks BOTH column A and row 1. $A1 locks column A only. A$1 locks row 1 only. Press F4 while editing a formula to quickly cycle through all reference modes.

workedExample.title: Worked Example: Calculating Ticket Fare with 18% GST
workedExample.text: Calculate Final Fare for 3 passengers with 18% GST rate stored in cell $C$1.
steps: Row 4: Passenger Rao, Base Fare in B4 = 5,000.
Formula for GST Amount in C4: =B4 * $C$1 → 5000 * 0.18 = 900.
Formula for Total Fare in D4: =B4 + C4 → 5,900.
When dragged to Row 5 (Base Fare = 7,000): Formula in C5 becomes =B5 * $C$1 (B5 updates to 7,000, but $C$1 remains locked to 0.18) → 1,260 GST.
workedExample.verdict: Absolute referencing prevents the dreaded '#VALUE!' or 0 error that happens when dragging relative references.

topics.memoryTrick: F4-LOCK: Press F4 once for Absolute ($A$1), twice for Row ($A$1), thrice for Column ($A1), fourth time to reset to Relative (A1).
topics.examTip: Common exam trap: If asked what happens if you drag =A1*$B$1 down one row: The formula becomes =A2*$B$1. A1 changes to A2 because it is relative; $B$1 stays fixed because it is absolute.

rule.title: The Three-Argument IF Rule
rule.text: Every IF statement requires three components separated by commas: =IF(Logical_Test, Value_if_True, Value_if_False). Text outcomes MUST be enclosed in quotation marks: e.g., =IF(D2>=85, 'ON-TIME', 'DELAYED').

workedExample.title: Worked Example: Automated Excess Baggage Surcharge Calculator
workedExample.text: A passenger on SkyLink Airways has a checked bag weighing 22 kg. Economy allowance is 15 kg; excess rate is ₹500 per kg.
steps: Cell B2 contains Baggage Weight = 22.
Step 1: Excel checks condition (22 > 15) → Evaluates to TRUE.
Step 2: Excel executes True branch: (22 - 15) * 500 = 7 * 500 = ₹3,500.
If Baggage was 14 kg: condition evaluates to FALSE → outputs ₹0 fee.

topics.partBanner: Part A · Internet Fundamentals & Information Literacy
topics.title: 1. Web Architecture, Secure Protocols (HTTPS) & Search Syntax
topics.premise: Aviation personnel access weather reports, NOTAMs (Notices to Air Missions), and regulatory mandates across web networks. Understanding URL architecture, encryption padlocks, and search operators is vital for fast, authentic information retrieval.

rows: URL Structure
https://www.dgca.gov.in/rules/car.html
Protocol (https), Subdomain (www), Domain (dgca.gov.in), Path (/rules/car.html)
Identifies exact web resource location; validates official government authenticity
HTTPS & SSL/TLS Padlock
https:// with padlock icon
Encrypts communication between user browser and web server
Guarantees passenger payment details and passport numbers cannot be intercepted in transit
Search Operator: site:
site:dgca.gov.in 'CAR Section 3'
Restricts search results exclusively to the specified official domain
Instantly pulls official Civil Aviation Requirements without commercial blog clutter
Search Operator: filetype:
filetype:pdf 'flight safety circular'
Filters search engine results to return only specific file formats (e.g., PDF)
Directly retrieves downloadable regulatory circulars and safety bulletin PDFs
Search Operator: Quotes ("")
"minimum equipment list" A320
Forces exact phrase matching in the specified order
Finds exact technical regulatory phrases rather than loose disconnected keyword hits
Browser Cache & History
Ctrl + Shift + Delete
Stores temporary web files and visited sites for fast reloading
Clearing cache resolves outdated weather radar loops and stuck flight booking portals

rule.title: The Secure Protocol Rule
rule.text: Never enter passenger credentials, payment card details, or flight dispatch logins on any website showing 'http://' (unsecured HTTP) or browser warning flags. Legitimate airline portals ALWAYS enforce 'https://' with a valid SSL/TLS certificate.

workedExample.title: Worked Example: Rapid Regulatory Lookup for Station Audit
workedExample.text: A station manager needs the latest DGCA circular on baggage compensation guidelines.
steps: Inefficient query: dgca baggage rules in india (returns 500,000 news articles and blogs).
Targeted Boolean query: site:dgca.gov.in filetype:pdf "passenger charter" baggage
Outcome: Result #1 is the exact official DGCA PDF circular with compensation fee tables.
Time taken: 3 seconds versus 20 minutes of filtering through irrelevant blogs.
workedExample.verdict: Advanced Boolean operators turn the search engine into an instant regulatory index.

topics.memoryTrick: U-R-L-S: Uniform Resource Locator Security: Check Protocol, Verify Domain, Restrict with site:, Filter with filetype:.
topics.examTip: In a 3-mark question on web security: Explain that HTTPS uses SSL/TLS encryption to protect sensitive data from eavesdropping (Man-in-the-Middle attacks), whereas HTTP transmits plain text that can be intercepted on open Wi-Fi.

topics.partBanner: Part B · Enterprise Email Communication & Etiquette
topics.title: 2. Professional Email Protocol, CC vs BCC & Passenger Data Privacy
topics.premise: Email is the legal backbone of airline enterprise communication. Misunderstanding CC versus BCC can cause massive data privacy breaches, while poor subject lines can stall ground handling coordination.

rows: To Field
Primary direct recipient(s) expected to take action or respond
To: Station_Manager@skylink.com regarding ramp staffing shortfall
Recipient is directly accountable for resolving the matter
Carbon Copy (CC)
Secondary recipient(s) included for situational awareness (no direct action required)
CC: Duty_Officer@skylink.com, Safety_Lead@skylink.com on incident report
All recipients see each other's email addresses
Blind Carbon Copy (BCC)
Hidden recipient(s); address is completely invisible to other recipients
BCC: 180 delayed passengers when emailing flight delay advisories
MANDATORY FOR PRIVACY: Prevents catastrophic passenger email leaks (GDPR/DPDP violation)
Subject Line
Clear, concise 5-8 word summary with flight/date/action tags
Subject: [URGENT] Flight SL-402 Delay Advisory & Gate Change - 14 Oct
Allows recipients to triage and prioritize urgent operational actions instantly
Email Signature
Standardized block: Full Name, Official Designation, Airline, Contact Details
Rohit Verma | Duty Manager | Ground Ops | Kempegowda Intl Airport
Establishes institutional authenticity and direct telephone contact
Attachment Hygiene
Attaching relevant compressed documentation with clean names
Attaching 'Incident_Report_AI402_14Oct.pdf' (under 10 MB)
Never attach executable files (.exe, .bat) or huge uncompressed archives

rule.title: The Strict BCC Privacy Rule
rule.text: When emailing multiple passengers or external vendors: NEVER put their email addresses in 'To' or 'CC'. ALWAYS use 'BCC'. Placing customer email addresses in CC exposes private contact details to strangers, violating aviation privacy laws and company data policies.

workedExample.title: Worked Example: Drafting an Operational Delay Notice to Passengers
workedExample.text: Draft an official flight rescheduling notice for passengers of Flight 6E 902.
steps: To: ops-notification@skylink.com (generic internal dummy address).
BCC: [List of all 160 passenger email addresses pasted here].
Subject: Operational Advisory: Flight SL 902 (BLR to DEL) Rescheduled - 14 Oct 2026.
Salutation: 'Dear Esteemed Passenger,'

Body: 'Please be advised that due to incoming airspace congestion, Flight SL 902 scheduled for departure at 14:30 hrs has been revised to 16:15 hrs. Gate open at 15:30 hrs. Refreshment vouchers are available at Counter 12.'
Sign-off: 'Sincerely, Ground Operations Team, SkyLink Airways'.
workedExample.verdict: Professional, courteous, operationally clear, and 100% compliant with privacy regulations.

topics.memoryTrick: B-C-C-P-R-I-V-A-C-Y: Blind Carbon Copy Protects Recipient Identity & Vital Aviation Confidentiality.
topics.examTip: A guaranteed exam question: What is the difference between CC and BCC? Answer: CC (Carbon Copy) displays recipient email addresses to everyone on the thread; BCC (Blind Carbon Copy) hides recipient addresses, protecting recipient privacy.

topics.partBanner: Part C · Cloud Drives & Aviation Cyber Safety
topics.title: 3. Cloud Collaboration, Cyber Threats (Phishing/Malware) & MFA Security
topics.premise: Airlines store shared shift handovers and flight plans on cloud drives (OneDrive, Google Drive). Ground workstations are prime targets for cyber attacks; staff must maintain vigilance against phishing, weak passwords, and unauthorized device connections.

rows: Cloud Sharing Permissions
View Only vs Commenter vs Editor permissions
Sharing live ground crew duty roster across terminal teams
Grant 'Editor' only to Duty Supervisors; all other staff receive 'View Only'
Phishing Attack
Fraudulent emails mimicking trusted authorities (DGCA, IT Support) to steal logins
Email pretending to be 'IT Helpdesk' demanding password reset via shady link
Never click links in unexpected emails; verify sender domain; report to Airline Cyber Security
Malware & Ransomware
Malicious software encrypting files or locking workstations for ransom
Infected USB drive inserted into dispatch terminal encrypts flight manifests
Strict policy banning unauthorized USB flash drives; continuous antivirus definitions
Strong Password Criteria
Minimum 12-16 characters: Uppercase, Lowercase, Numbers, and Special Symbols
Securing airline check-in terminal user accounts against brute force attacks
Use passphrase sentences (e.g., 'SkyFly#2026@BLR!Safe'); never reuse passwords
Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
Requires 2+ verification factors: Password + OTP/Authenticator App prompt
Accessing airline crew scheduling portal from mobile or remote tablet
Even if password is stolen in a phishing attempt, attacker cannot log in without the physical OTP token
Public / Apron Wi-Fi Hygiene
Unencrypted open Wi-Fi networks subject to packet sniffing and spoofing
Ground agent checking company flight schedules on airport public Wi-Fi
Always connect via corporate Virtual Private Network (VPN); never disable firewall

rule.title: The Zero-Trust USB & Password Rule
rule.text: 1. NEVER plug personal USB pen drives into airport operational workstations. 2. NEVER share your terminal user password with colleagues or write it on sticky notes. Every agent is legally liable for actions logged under their user ID.

workedExample.title: Worked Example: Identifying a Spear-Phishing Email Attempt
workedExample.text: A ticketing agent receives an email: 'URGENT from DGCA: Your Airport Pass has been revoked. Click here immediately to verify credentials: http://dgca-verification-portal.xyz/login'.
steps: Red Flag 1: False urgency ('Click immediately or pass revoked').
Red Flag 2: Suspicious sender domain (dgca-verification-portal.xyz instead of official dgca.gov.in).
Red Flag 3: Unsecured HTTP link instead of official HTTPS.
Correct Action: Do NOT click the link. Take a screenshot, forward email to airline Cyber Security Ops, and notify supervisor.
workedExample.verdict: Vigilant staff response halts potential cyber intrusion into the airport reservation network.

topics.memoryTrick: P-A-S-S-W-O-R-D: Phishing awareness, Authentication MFA, Share links with expiry, Strong passwords, Wi-Fi security, OS updates, Regular backups, Defense vigilance.
topics.examTip: In a 5-mark question on Cyber Threats: Define Phishing (social engineering email deception), Ransomware (malware that encrypts operational data for ransom), and MFA (two-factor authentication combining something you know + something you have).

quickRevision.rememberThis: HTTPS uses SSL/TLS encryption (padlock icon) to prevent data interception; HTTP transmits plain text.
site: limits search to one domain (site:dgca.gov.in); filetype: filters format (filetype:pdf); quotes enforce exact phrase.
CC reveals email addresses to all recipients; BCC hides addresses to protect passenger personal privacy.
False urgency, generic greeting, mismatched sender domain, unsecure links, and grammar errors.
Combines 2 factors: Something you know (password) + Something you have (phone OTP/token) for secure login.
